image_query: Hoysaleswara Temple Halebidu wall frieze relief sculpture close-up
tweets: Hoysaleśvara Temple, Halebidu — begun c. 1121 CE under Hoysala king Viṣṇuvardhana. Its walls are chloritic schist, soft as quarried, hardening in air — soft enough to carve every bead on a dancer's necklace.

Six horizontal friezes wrap the plinth — elephants, lions, horsemen, scrollwork, mythical beasts, then swans — before panels retell the Rāmāyaṇa and Mahābhārata in stone. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
